ja: 決済のバグが直るまで、リリース日の発表は見合わせましょう。
en: Let's hold off on announcing the release date until the payment bug is fixed.
alternatives: Let's hold off on announcing the release date until we've fixed the payment bug.
Let's wait to announce the release date until the payment bug is fixed.
Why don't we hold off on announcing the release date until the payment bug gets fixed?
point: hold off on の後は動名詞。until 節は未来でも現在形

ja: 先週のリリースで、私たちはついにダークモードを追加しました。
en: In last week's release, we finally added dark mode.
alternatives: We finally added dark mode in last week's release.
We finally shipped dark mode in the release last week.
point: 過去の一時点の出来事なので現在完了ではなく過去形

ja: ユーザーは、このアプリで写真を共有できません。
en: Users can't share photos in this app.
alternatives: Users can't share photos with this app.
Users cannot share photos on this app.
point: 「できない」は can't＋動詞の原形

ja: お客さんから一番よく頼まれる機能は、今回のリリースには入らないんです。
en: The feature that customers ask for most won't be in this release.
alternatives: The feature customers request most won't be in this release.
The feature that our customers ask for most isn't going to be in this release.
point: ask for の for を関係詞節の中で落とさない

ja: このアプリにオフラインモードがあればいいのに。出張中によく必要になるんです。
en: I wish this app had an offline mode. I often need it on business trips.
alternatives: I wish the app had an offline mode. I often need one when I'm on business trips.
If only this app had an offline mode. I often need it when I travel for work.
point: 現在の願望は wish の後を過去形（had）にする

ja: うちのマネージャーは、ユーザーが本当に欲しいのは新機能じゃなくて読み込みの速さだと考えています。
en: Our manager thinks that what users really want is faster loading, not new features.
alternatives: Our manager believes what users really want is faster loading rather than new features.
Our manager thinks users really want faster load times, not new features.
point: 「〜が欲しいもの」は what users want を主語にする

ja: ベータ版のテストが終わったら、その機能を正式に出すかどうか決めよう。
en: Let's decide whether to officially launch that feature once the beta testing is over.
alternatives: When the beta testing is done, let's decide if we should officially release that feature.
Let's decide whether we'll officially roll out that feature after the beta testing is finished.
point: 未来のことでも「終わったら」の節は現在形 is over

ja: 営業チームに、機能の要望を一つのリストにまとめるよう頼んでもらえますか？
en: Could you ask the sales team to put their feature requests in one list?
alternatives: Can you ask the sales team to collect their feature requests in a single list?
Could you ask the sales team to gather all their feature requests into one list?
point: ask + 人 + to do の語順。that 節にしない

ja: たとえユーザーからの要望が多くても、その機能は今回のリリースには入れられません。
en: Even if a lot of users ask for it, we can't include that feature in this release.
alternatives: Even if many users request it, we can't add that feature to this release.
We can't put that feature in this release, even if lots of users want it.
point: 「たとえ〜でも」は even if、even though ではない

ja: お忙しいところすみませんが、エクスポート機能を次のスプリントに入れていただけないかと思いまして。
en: Sorry to bother you, but I was wondering if you could fit the export feature into the next sprint.
alternatives: Sorry to bother you, but I was wondering whether you could add the export feature to the next sprint.
I'm sorry to trouble you, but I was wondering if the export feature could go into the next sprint.
point: I was wondering if で依頼を柔らかくする

ja: もしうちにエンジニアがあと二人いたら、あなたなら検索機能を先に作りますか？
en: If we had two more engineers, would you build the search feature first?
alternatives: If we had two extra engineers, would you build search first?
Would you build the search feature first if we had two more engineers?
point: 仮定の話は if 節を過去形、主節を would にする

ja: PM は、決済機能のリリースは来月までずれ込むかもしれないと言っていました。
en: The PM said the payment feature release might be pushed back until next month.
alternatives: The PM said the release of the payment feature might slip to next month.
The PM told us the payment feature might not be released until next month.
point: said に合わせて may ではなく might にする

ja: うちが先月ダークモードを優先していたら、今ごろこんなにサポートへの問い合わせは来ていないでしょうね。
en: If we had prioritized dark mode last month, we wouldn't be getting so many support requests now.
alternatives: If we'd prioritized dark mode last month, we probably wouldn't be getting this many support tickets now.
Had we made dark mode a priority last month, we wouldn't be getting so many support requests right now.
point: 過去の仮定は had + 過去分詞、今の結果は would be

ja: サラ、その機能要望、次のスプリントまで後回しにしてもらえる？
en: Sara, could you put off that feature request until the next sprint?
alternatives: Sara, can you push that feature request back to the next sprint?
Sara, could you hold off on that feature request until the next sprint?
point: 「後回しにする」は put off / push back で言える
